questions.q: The elevator is the second surface in the geometry (`CA_SV_CS1`). Which function number goes into `PWM_AUX_FUNC6` to put it on output AUX6?
questions.explain: Surface CA_SV_CS1 is the second actuator of type "servo", that is, Servo 2. Servos take numbers 201…215 (in 1.18; before 1.18 they were 201…208, output_functions.yaml), so 202. 102 is Motor 2, 302 Peripheral via Actuator Set 2, 402 RC Roll.

questions.q: Pixhawk 6X (fmu-v6x), PX4 1.18. What is wrong in this fragment?
questions.fragment:
PWM_AUX_TIM0   -3
PWM_AUX_TIM1   50
PWM_AUX_FUNC1  101
PWM_AUX_FUNC2  102
PWM_AUX_FUNC3  103
PWM_AUX_FUNC4  201
PWM_AUX_FUNC5  104
options: Servo 1 sits in the DShot600 group with the motors
Motor 4 on AUX5: Timer4 has no DMA, so DShot is impossible there
The value −3 does not exist in 1.18; DShot600 is −2
Function 201 cannot be assigned to FMU outputs, only MAIN
questions.explain: AUX1–4 hang off Timer5, one group with PWM_AUX_TIM0 = −3 (DShot600): the servo on AUX4 will get DShot frames instead of a 50 Hz pulse. Motor 4 on AUX5 with TIM1 = 50 will not work right either, but not because of DMA: Timer4 has DMA. −2 was DShot1200 in 1.15 and was removed in 1.16. 1.18 added −6…−8, the same speeds with bidirectional DShot.

questions.q: An output whose function used to be Disabled was assigned Motor 1 (PWM). What does the `pwm_out` driver write by itself?
questions.explain: PWMOut::update_params, at the moment an output's function changes from Disabled to Motor on running firmware, sets MIN 1100 and MAX 1900; DIS stays 1000. DIS = 1500 and the group switching from 400 to 50 Hz is the automation for Servo, and the rate changes only if the group had no function before.

questions.q: A servo on an IO output: `MIN` = 1000, `MAX` = 2000, the output's bit in `PWM_MAIN_REV` is set. The allocator outputs +0.5. How many microseconds on the output?
questions.explain: Reversal flips the sign of the value before conversion: −0.5. Then MIN + (v + 1)/2 · (MAX − MIN) = 1000 + 0.25 · 1000 = 1250. Without reversal it would be 1750.

questions.q: `PWM_AUX_REV` = 10. Which outputs have their range reversed?
questions.explain: 10 = 8 + 2 = bits 3 and 1. Bit n−1 is output n, so outputs 4 and 2. AUX1 and AUX3 would give mask 5.

questions.q: A hexacopter on a Pixhawk 6X, PX4 1.18: motors on AUX1–6, `PWM_AUX_TIM0` = `PWM_AUX_TIM1` = −6 (BDShot600). Which outputs get bidirectional DShot with RPM?
questions.explain: In 1.18 bidirectional DShot is chosen per timer group: −6 on TIM0 (Timer5, AUX1–4) and on TIM1 (Timer4, AUX5–6), and both timers have DMA. The STM32 driver triggers the groups in turn and reads the RPM of one channel of the group per cycle (dshot.c, v1.18.0); the "timer 0 only" limitation is gone. In 1.16–1.17 with `DSHOT_BIDIR_EN` = 1 DShot stayed only on the timer with index 0, and AUX5–6 got no signal. Timer12 (AUX7–8) has no DMA and cannot do DShot. This combination was not tested on hardware.

questions.q: A control surface servo on an IO output: `MIN` = 1000, `MAX` = 1800, `DIS` = 1500, `FAIL` = −1. Flight termination fired. What is on the output?
questions.explain: FAIL = −1 means the value by function; for Servo that is 0, the midpoint between MIN and MAX: (1000 + 1800)/2 = 1400. The output would get DIS = 1500 on kill or when disarmed. Only Parachute and Constant Max get MAX by default.

questions.q: By the PX4 sign rule a positive command raises the trailing edge. What are the coefficients of the **right** elevon?
questions.explain: The right elevon edge goes up: the right wing loses lift and goes down, a roll to the right, positive. At the same time the rear of the wing pushes down, nose up, positive pitch. That is what the 3000_generic_wing airframe has: CA_SV_CS1_TRQ_R 0.5, CA_SV_CS1_TRQ_P 0.5. The −0.5/+0.5 option is the left elevon.

questions.q: An output has the Peripheral via Actuator Set 2 (302) function. Which command lets a companion switch it to maximum?
questions.explain: FunctionActuatorSet reads VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR (187): param1…param6 are the −1…1 values for Peripheral 1…6, param7 is the set index, and only 0 is accepted. NaN in a parameter leaves the output as it was. This function does not handle DO_SET_SERVO, and DO_GRIPPER drives the Gripper function (430).

questions.q: A plane on the bench, disarmed: in Manual the control surfaces do not follow the sticks, but the Actuators sliders work. Which parameter explains this?
questions.explain: With COM_PREARM_MODE = 0 there is no prearm state: when disarmed every output sits at DIS, and the servo value is not used. Value 2 enables prearm 5 s after boot, and the servos (but not the motors) start working. 400 Hz is the wrong rate for an analog servo, but the surfaces would still move. The sliders work because in 1.18 output testing is always allowed (before 1.18 COM_MOT_TEST_EN = 0 could forbid it).
